method: After freezing the pair, returned first to Article 16.5 and the current official catalogue, then the exchange and thesis rules, before reconsidering the UCR evidence and audience text.
findings: The standard full-time English programme has no formal route. Years one and two each contain eight required 6.5 EC courses and two 4 EC skills courses. The third year comprises 26 EC of study abroad, two restricted 6.5 EC choices, a 13 EC research project or regional internship, and an 8 EC individual thesis. There is no unrestricted elective block. The official table resolves the ambiguous general wording by showing a separate menu in periods four and five. People Analytics and Data and Analytics for Good are valid first-listed examples, each 6.5 EC and listed in the corresponding period. The documented plan retains the restricted menus and both permitted capstone choices rather than implying a specialist track.

A standard completion of all 60 first-year EC satisfies the 47 EC BSA floor and satisfies the exchange eligibility requirements of 53.5 EC at application and 60 EC before departure. There is no BSA condition on a named course for this degree. Partner selection, language or content criteria and IRO approval apply. The standard 26 EC exchange is required; a 4 EC summer or winter course or 6.5 EC internship may replace a limited part under their rules, without combining the substitutions. The non-exchange timing footnote describes when the regional internship and thesis may run, while the EER governs any exception to the requirement. The ordinary project track uses EBP2001 in periods four and five, with team research agendas split into individual thesis work packages. EBP2003 has approval requirements and a report and presentation. EBT0017 is a distinct 8 EC independently written final paper. Verified the published project, thesis and example elective entries for credits and checked their prerequisite fields. The 20 core entries list high-school mathematics for EBC1051, EBC1051 before EBC1052, and calculus, linear algebra, optimisation and strong mathematical skills for EBC2198. The programming entry gives skills and subject names without specific module codes. The scheduled first-year mathematics and decision theory supply that preparation, and no later compulsory course is identified as an entry dependency. General enrolment and syllabus rules remain applicable. First-year tutorial attendance is 75% with an assignment route for compensation. Attendance and registration do not add credits.

The first-listed restricted examples are in different periods, with the project running alongside both and the distinct thesis completing the final semester. The course catalogue lists the same project and thesis credit values as the adopted EER. The research project’s own description verifies the research-agenda and individual work-package structure. Introduction to Data Science expressly uses R for cleaning and visualising data, while the Maastricht skills course adds a dedicated RMarkdown and tidyverse sequence. Money, Banking & Finance expressly includes derivative pricing and bank risk, so the former claim that derivatives are absent was corrected. Programming and applied data preparation now both precede Machine Learning; Deep Learning follows in the final term. These substantive links justify the qualified option while preserving the specialisation and assessment gaps.
